title: Top-down PLM assembly with multi-timescale adaptive state and bottom-up causal ablation
question: Does a compact multi-timescale persistent state improve history-conditioned exact decision capability when embedded in a complete persistent-state -> router -> executor -> verifier loop, compared with matched no-state, single-timescale, and reduced-timescale controls?
hypothesis: A fixed multi-timescale adaptive state bank provides decision-useful temporal contrasts that a matched single-timescale state cannot represent efficiently, improving held-out exact history-conditioned capability while using the same learned policy capacity and explicitly accounted state computation.

endpoints.name: exact_class_balanced_success
endpoints.description: Exact generated action success on balanced held-out paired-history episodes; primary decision is evaluated at H=256.

endpoints.name: history_conditioned_action_gap
endpoints.description: Fraction of paired histories with identical current observation and opposite correct actions for which the model selects different actions.

endpoints.name: state_intervention_effect
endpoints.description: Change in exact success and paired action gap when a frozen trained MTSK policy receives reset or swapped persistent state.

endpoints.name: total_computation_work
endpoints.description: Explicit evaluation work including state updates, router arithmetic and verification; state work may not be omitted.

endpoints.name: persistent_state_footprint
endpoints.description: Number of persistent state scalars carried to the decision.

endpoints.name: train_compute_work
endpoints.description: Measured training arithmetic proxy for the identical policy optimizer schedule across trained arms.

decision_rule.condition: At H=256, MTSK improves exact_class_balanced_success over single_timescale by more than the preregistered materiality threshold and the seed-bootstrap 95% confidence interval for the paired seed-level difference excludes zero; MTSK must also exceed no_state.
decision_rule.licenses: bounded evidence that the registered multi-timescale state representation improves exact history-conditioned capability on the finite synthetic benchmark under matched policy capacity and explicit state-computation accounting.
decision_rule.does_not_license: biological equivalence, general intelligence, asymptotic scaling, real-world multimodal competence, or hardware speedup.

decision_rule.condition: MTSK produces a material history-conditioned action gap but does not improve exact_class_balanced_success over single_timescale.
decision_rule.licenses: the multi-timescale state changes history-dependent behavior but the registered capability advantage is not established.

decision_rule.condition: MTSK matches or loses to single_timescale within the preregistered materiality threshold.
decision_rule.licenses: the registered multi-timescale advantage is not supported on this benchmark.
decision_rule.does_not_license: failure of persistent state generally, failure of multi-timescale memory generally, or failure on other environments.

interpretation_order: representability of temporal relation through state map
held_constant: benchmark generator version and disjoint train/test seed streams
optimizer family, learning rate and training step count
state footprint of three scalar slots
evaluation sample count and paired-history construction
